title: Case Book: Early, Late and Just-in-Time Vehicle Inspections on Wayfare Agreements
content:
This case book applies the clock-start rule of the **Driver Services Agreements and Account Standing** product, which sets the day a passed vehicle inspection's validity runs from and so changes the inspection validity days: the calendar days from the inspection date for which the inspection counts as the vehicle inspection on file.

## Clock-start rule

- For an inspection passed while the inspection on file still had at least 7 days to run, counted from the inspection date to the expiry date on file, the inspection validity days run from that expiry date, so the days between the inspection date and the expiry date on file are added to the inspection validity days.
- For an inspection passed after the inspection on file had expired, they run from the inspection date, and the inspection validity days lose the days the inspection on file had been expired, at most 30 days.
- For an inspection passed while the inspection on file had not expired but had fewer than 7 days to run, they run from the inspection date and the inspection validity days are taken unchanged.

The expiry date on file is the vehicle inspection expiry date on the agreement as it stands before the new inspection is recorded.

## Cases (hypothetical, inspection date 2026-03-02)

| Case | Inspection expiry date on file | Days from the inspection date to it | Effect on the inspection validity days |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 2026-03-20 | 18 | 18 added |
| 2 | 2026-03-09 | 7 | 7 added |
| 3 | 2026-03-08 | 6 | unchanged |
| 4 | 2026-03-02 | 0 (expires on the inspection date) | unchanged |
| 5 | 2026-02-20 | expired 10 days earlier | 10 lost |
| 6 | 2026-01-01 | expired 60 days earlier | 30 lost (the most that is lost) |

Case 2 is the first day on which the early-inspection branch applies; case 4 has not expired, because the expiry date is the inspection date itself.
